decision.title: Remove upstream repository reference
decision.context: After initial fork setup, we considered whether to keep or remove the upstream remote to reduce the chance of accidentally interacting with the original repository.

option.name: Keep upstream remote for easy syncing
option.cons: Risk of accidental interaction with upstream repository

option.name: Remove upstream remote for isolation
option.pros: Complete isolation from original repository, simplified workflow
option.cons: Manual process needed if syncing with original repository later

decision.rationale: Prioritize safety of avoiding accidental interactions with upstream over convenience of syncing

steps.step: Removed the upstream remote with `git remote remove upstream`
Verified only fork remains as a remote
Updated documentation to reflect this decision

decision.title: Repository fork setup
decision.context: Need to set up development on a forked repository while maintaining ability to sync with upstream

option.name: Work directly on upstream with branch permissions
Work on fork with upstream sync
option.pros: Full control over fork, clean PR process

decision.chosen: Work on fork with upstream sync
decision.rationale: Provides more flexibility and adheres to best practice for open source contributions

steps.step: Configure git remote to point to fork

decision.title: Handle nil GroupedLight pointers
decision.context: A runtime panic occurs in the `set room` command when attempting to call `Set()` on a nil `GroupedLight` pointer. This happens when a room returned by the Hue API doesn't have an associated GroupedLight service.

option.name: Add nil check in the caller
option.pros: - Fails fast, close to where the error occurs - Provides specific user feedback about which room has the issue - No change to method signatures or contracts
option.cons: - Must be implemented in all calling code

option.name: Handle nil receiver in the Set method
option.pros: - Centralized fix for all callers - More defensive programming approach
option.cons: - Less specific error messaging - Changes method contract - Obscures actual issue from callers

decision.chosen: Add nil check in the caller
decision.rationale: Following the principle of failing fast and providing clear user feedback. This approach also maintains the original contract of the Set method and makes the limitation explicit at the call site rather than hiding it in the method implementation.

steps.step: Added nil check before calling `Set()` in `cmd/set/set_room.go`
Added appropriate warning message for users
Added similar nil check in `cmd/get/get_room.go` to prevent similar issues
